prompts.label: WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: How do access pattern and retrieval tolerance affect S3 cost?

reveal.text: S3 storage classes trade storage price, retrieval price, minimum storage duration, availability characteristics, and retrieval latency. S3 Intelligent-Tiering is useful when object access patterns are unknown or change over time; lifecycle rules are useful when the age-based transition pattern is known.

prompts.label: READ THE CONFIG
prompts.placeholder: Click the important parts of this configuration before revealing the explanation.

annotations.title: Age-based transition
annotations.explanation: Lifecycle rules can move objects to a lower-cost class after a defined age.

annotations.title: Archive transition
annotations.explanation: Archive tiers reduce storage cost when slower retrieval and retrieval charges are acceptable.

prompts.label: EXAM CLUE
prompts.placeholder: What phrase should make this answer jump out?

items: unknown/changing access -> S3 Intelligent-Tiering
known age-based transition -> lifecycle rule
long retention + rare retrieval -> archive tier

source_refs.title: AWS Certified Solutions Architect - Associate (SAA-C03) exam guide

glossary.definition: A fee that can apply when data is read back from some lower-cost storage tiers.
A minimum billable storage period that can make short-lived data expensive in some archival or infrequent-access classes.
An S3 rule that automatically transitions or expires objects based on age or other configured conditions.

prompts.label: WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: What should this concept make you think of?

reveal.text: gp3 decouples baseline storage size from provisioned IOPS and throughput, while io2 targets demanding IOPS and st1 or sc1 target lower-cost sequential throughput workloads.

prompts.label: WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: Which performance requirement justifies paying for each EBS option?

items: gp3: general-purpose SSD where IOPS and throughput can be tuned without choosing io2.
io2: demanding workloads where high, predictable provisioned IOPS justify the higher cost.
st1: frequently accessed large sequential throughput.
sc1: lowest-cost HDD for infrequently accessed sequential data.

prompts.label: EXAM CLUE
prompts.placeholder: What phrase should make this answer jump out?

items: general-purpose SSD -> gp3
high predictable IOPS -> io2
frequent sequential throughput -> st1
cold sequential data -> sc1

nodes.title: Cost-aware storage migration and managed transfer

prompts.label: WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: What should this concept make you think of?

reveal.text: Data-transfer cost depends on how data moves and whether access is one-time or ongoing. DataSync is a managed online transfer and data-movement service. AWS Transfer Family provides managed file transfer endpoints such as SFTP. Storage Gateway supports ongoing hybrid storage access. Snow Family remains useful for SAA exam recognition as the traditional AWS physical/offline transfer family, but Snow Family devices are no longer available to new customers.

prompts.label: WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: Choose the service from the transfer pattern and current availability.

items: Managed online copy between supported storage systems -> AWS DataSync.
Managed SFTP/FTPS/FTP/AS2 file-transfer endpoint -> AWS Transfer Family.
Ongoing hybrid storage interface -> AWS Storage Gateway.
Exam-recognition of the traditional AWS physical appliance -> Snow Family; for a new real-world design, use current AWS alternatives because new customers cannot order Snow Family devices.

prompts.label: EXAM CLUE
prompts.placeholder: What phrase should make this answer jump out?

items: online storage copy -> DataSync
managed SFTP -> Transfer Family
hybrid storage interface -> Storage Gateway
legacy/offline appliance exam clue -> Snow Family

nodes.title: Storage access, sizing, backup, and archival economics

prompts.label: WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: Which storage requirements change who pays and how much capacity is kept?

reveal.text: Cost optimization starts with the storage access pattern and required durability/recovery behavior. S3 Requester Pays can shift eligible request and download costs to requesters. S3 and EFS avoid fixed block volume sizing, while EBS capacity is explicitly provisioned. Backup and archive retention should keep only the recovery history the business or compliance requirement actually needs.

prompts.label: COMPARE
prompts.placeholder: Map each cost problem to the storage design response.

cells.requirement: Large shared S3 dataset; consumers should pay download/request charges
EC2 block volume is consistently overprovisioned
Shared file capacity changes significantly over time
cells.choice: Evaluate elastic file storage such as EFS

cells.requirement: Backups are kept far longer than business recovery needs
cells.choice: Align backup retention/archive tier with RPO/compliance need

prompts.label: EXAM CLUE
prompts.placeholder: What wording should trigger storage-cost reasoning?

items: requester should pay -> S3 Requester Pays
overprovisioned EBS -> right-size
unknown file capacity -> elastic file storage
excess backup history -> retention policy

source_refs.title: AWS Certified Solutions Architect - Associate (SAA-C03) exam guide

Amazon EBS volume types

glossary.definition: An S3 setting where the requester pays eligible request and data-download charges instead of the bucket owner.
How frequently and in what way data is read or written, which strongly affects the cheapest suitable storage choice.
Long-term storage optimized for low storage cost when retrieval can be slower or less frequent.

nodes.title: On-Demand, Savings Plans, Reserved Instances, and Spot

prompts.label: WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: What should this concept make you think of?

reveal.text: On-Demand provides maximum pricing flexibility with no long-term commitment. Compute Savings Plans commit to a consistent amount of compute spend and can apply across EC2, Fargate, and Lambda; EC2 Instance Savings Plans are more specific to an instance family in a Region. Reserved Instances remain an EC2 pricing option tied more closely to instance configuration. Spot uses spare EC2 capacity at a deep discount, but a Spot interruption can reclaim the instance. Pricing commitments and capacity reservation are related exam concepts but should not be treated as the same requirement.

prompts.label: COMPARE
prompts.placeholder: The choices are visible. Reveal the differences one cell at a time.

cells.fit: Short-lived, new, or unpredictable baseline usage

cells.commitment: Hourly spend commitment; broad compute flexibility
cells.fit: Stable eligible compute spend while services/Regions/families may change
Stable EC2 family usage where a stronger commitment is acceptable
Existing RI-specific exam or capacity/pricing requirements

prompts.label: EXAM CLUE
prompts.placeholder: What phrase should make this answer jump out?

items: interruptible -> Spot
broad EC2/Fargate/Lambda commitment -> Compute Savings Plan
EC2 family + Region commitment -> EC2 Instance Savings Plan
no commitment -> On-Demand

source_refs.title: AWS Certified Solutions Architect - Associate (SAA-C03) exam guide

glossary.definition: An agreement to a defined level or configuration of usage for a term in exchange for discounted pricing.
An event where AWS reclaims Spot capacity, so the workload must tolerate instance loss or interruption.
Reserved EC2 capacity in an Availability Zone. A pricing discount and a capacity reservation are separate concepts.

nodes.title: Right-sizing, Auto Scaling, and Compute Optimizer

prompts.label: WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: What should this concept make you think of?

reveal.text: Right-sizing matches resource capacity to measured demand, while Auto Scaling adjusts capacity over time. AWS Compute Optimizer uses historical utilization data over a lookback period to produce optimization recommendations for supported resources.

prompts.label: WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: When is right-sizing different from Auto Scaling?

items: A resource is consistently oversized for its measured workload -> right-size it.
Demand changes over time -> use elastic scaling to add and remove capacity.
You need utilization-based recommendation candidates -> evaluate AWS Compute Optimizer.
Measure performance risk as well as savings before applying a smaller recommendation.

prompts.label: EXAM CLUE
prompts.placeholder: What phrase should make this answer jump out?

items: consistently underutilized -> right-size
demand changes over time -> Auto Scaling
recommendation based on utilization -> Compute Optimizer

source_refs.title: AWS Certified Solutions Architect - Associate (SAA-C03) exam guide
What is AWS Compute Optimizer?

glossary.definition: Matching resource size to measured workload demand instead of keeping unnecessary CPU, memory, or storage capacity.
The historical utilization window analyzed when producing a recommendation.

nodes.title: Lambda, Fargate, and EC2 cost trade-offs

prompts.label: WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: What should this concept make you think of?

reveal.text: Lambda and Fargate follow a pay per use model based on requests, duration, or provisioned task resources, while EC2 charges for running instance capacity. Serverless designs can reduce idle capacity for bursty or intermittent workloads, but steady high-utilization workloads still need a real cost comparison.

prompts.label: WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: Which execution pattern makes each compute model cost-effective?

items: Short-lived event-driven work with idle periods -> Lambda can avoid continuously running server capacity.
Container workload without worker-server management -> Fargate trades server management for per-task resource pricing.
Steady high utilization with infrastructure control needs -> EC2 may be economical, especially with suitable commitments.
Do not choose serverless only because it sounds cheaper; compare utilization, duration, concurrency, and operational requirements.

prompts.label: EXAM CLUE
prompts.placeholder: What phrase should make this answer jump out?

items: AWS Lambda
Lambda, Fargate, and EC2 cost trade-offs

source_refs.title: AWS Certified Solutions Architect - Associate (SAA-C03) exam guide

glossary.definition: A pricing model where cost follows actual requests, duration, or provisioned task resources instead of a continuously running server fleet.
Provisioned compute that is running but not doing useful work.

nodes.title: Availability, hibernation, and elastic compute cost

prompts.label: WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: How can availability requirements change the cheapest compute design?

reveal.text: Cost-effective compute matches availability to workload class. Production workloads may justify continuous multi-AZ capacity, while development or test workloads can often stop or scale in when unused. EC2 hibernation preserves RAM state on EBS and does not incur instance usage charges while the instance is in the stopped state, although EBS storage and other attached resources can still cost money.

prompts.label: COMPARE
prompts.placeholder: Choose the cost control from workload behavior.

cells.case: Dev/test is unused nights and weekends
cells.response: Stop or schedule capacity off when acceptable

cells.case: EC2 application takes a long time to rebuild in-memory state
Traffic varies predictably or by demand
cells.response: Auto Scale rather than keep peak capacity always running
Do not remove required redundancy merely to reduce cost

prompts.label: EXAM CLUE
prompts.placeholder: What phrases should trigger these decisions?

items: non-production idle window -> stop/schedule
resume RAM state -> hibernate
variable demand -> Auto Scaling
required HA -> preserve redundancy

source_refs.title: AWS Certified Solutions Architect - Associate (SAA-C03) exam guide
Hibernate your Amazon EC2 instance

glossary.definition: Suspend an EC2 instance to EBS while preserving RAM state so it can resume later.
Development, test, staging, or other workloads that often do not need full production-level continuous capacity.
Reduce running capacity when demand falls.

nodes.title: RDS, Aurora Serverless v2, and DynamoDB cost models

prompts.label: WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: What should this concept make you think of?

reveal.text: Database cost should follow access pattern and capacity predictability. RDS uses provisioned database instances and storage. Aurora Serverless v2 can scale ACUs within a configured range. DynamoDB on-demand capacity avoids explicit RCU/WCU provisioning for variable traffic, while provisioned capacity can fit predictable throughput.

prompts.label: COMPARE
prompts.placeholder: Choose the database capacity model from traffic predictability.

prompts.label: EXAM CLUE
prompts.placeholder: What phrase should make this answer jump out?

items: variable relational capacity -> Aurora Serverless v2
unpredictable DynamoDB traffic -> on-demand
predictable DynamoDB throughput -> provisioned

glossary.definition: Aurora capacity unit. A unit of Aurora Serverless v2 compute and memory capacity.
A DynamoDB capacity mode where AWS handles request throughput without you provisioning RCU/WCU values.
A DynamoDB capacity mode where read and write capacity are configured explicitly.

prompts.label: WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: What should this concept make you think of?

reveal.text: A cache can absorb repeated reads and reduce database CPU, I/O, and capacity requirements when the workload has cacheable access patterns. A cache hit avoids a database read; a cache miss still reaches the database.

prompts.label: WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: When does adding a cache actually reduce database cost?

items: Many requests repeatedly read the same cacheable data.
Database CPU/I/O is driven by repeated reads that a cache can absorb.
The application can tolerate the required cache freshness/invalidation behavior.
Do not add a cache solely for cost if the workload has poor cache reuse.

prompts.label: EXAM CLUE
prompts.placeholder: What phrase should make this answer jump out?

items: ElastiCache

glossary.definition: A request served from the cache instead of the database.
A request that must go to the database because the needed item is not in the cache.

prompts.label: WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: What should this concept make you think of?

reveal.text: Backup frequency and retention determine recovery coverage and storage consumption, so retention should match business and compliance requirements.

prompts.label: WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: How should backup retention be optimized without weakening recovery requirements?

items: Keep enough recovery points to satisfy business RPO/RTO and compliance.
Expire obsolete snapshots/backups instead of keeping every recovery point indefinitely.
Use longer retention only when the recovery or compliance requirement actually needs it.

prompts.label: EXAM CLUE

items: retention period

nodes.title: Database connections, read scaling, and migration cost

prompts.label: WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: Which database mechanisms reduce unnecessary capacity or migration effort?

reveal.text: RDS Proxy maintains a connection pool and reuses database connections so bursty applications do not require the database to absorb the full client-connection count. Read replicas can move read traffic away from the writer when read demand is the bottleneck. A homogeneous migration keeps the same database engine, while a heterogeneous migration changes engines and may need schema/code conversion. AWS DMS moves database data, and DMS Schema Conversion helps with heterogeneous migrations.

prompts.label: COMPARE
prompts.placeholder: Choose the mechanism from the actual database cost driver.

cells.problem: Thousands of short-lived connections create DB overhead
Read-only traffic is driving primary DB capacity
Move data to an equivalent database engine
Move between different engines and convert schema

prompts.label: EXAM CLUE
prompts.placeholder: What wording should trigger these choices?

items: connection exhaustion -> RDS Proxy
read-heavy -> read replica
same engine migration -> DMS data migration
different engine/schema -> DMS Schema Conversion

nodes.title: NAT gateway and VPC endpoint cost trade-offs

prompts.label: WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: What should this concept make you think of?

reveal.text: NAT gateways have an hourly charge plus a per-GB data processing charge. Sending traffic across AZs to a NAT gateway can add cross-AZ data-transfer cost. S3 and DynamoDB gateway endpoints have no additional endpoint charge and can avoid NAT processing for supported traffic. Interface endpoints have their own hourly and data-processing charges, so they should be compared against the NAT path rather than assumed cheaper.

prompts.label: COMPARE
prompts.placeholder: The choices are visible. Reveal the differences one cell at a time.

cells.cost: Hourly + per-GB processing; cross-AZ path can add transfer cost

cells.fit: VPC traffic to S3/DynamoDB without NAT
PrivateLink-supported service where private ENI connectivity is needed

prompts.label: EXAM CLUE
prompts.placeholder: What phrase should make this answer jump out?

items: large S3/DynamoDB NAT traffic -> gateway endpoint
cross-AZ NAT traffic -> same-AZ NAT path / evaluate per-AZ NAT
interface endpoint -> compare endpoint cost with NAT cost

source_refs.title: AWS Certified Solutions Architect - Associate (SAA-C03) exam guide

Gateway endpoints

glossary.definition: A per-data-volume charge applied by some networking services in addition to hourly charges.
A no-additional-charge VPC endpoint type for S3 and DynamoDB that uses route tables.
A VPC endpoint that creates private network interfaces and has PrivateLink-related hourly and data-processing pricing.

nodes.title: Data transfer and edge caching cost

prompts.label: WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: What should this concept make you think of?

reveal.text: Architecture choices that keep traffic local or serve cacheable content from edge locations can reduce origin load and some data-transfer paths.

prompts.label: WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: When can an edge cache reduce cost as well as latency?

items: Many users repeatedly request the same cacheable content.
CloudFront can serve cache hits without repeatedly fetching the object from the origin.
Measure cache hit ratio and origin/data-transfer costs before assuming the CDN saves money.

prompts.label: EXAM CLUE
prompts.placeholder: What phrase should make this answer jump out?

items: CloudFront
Data transfer and edge caching cost

glossary.definition: The backend source from which a CDN retrieves content when the content is not already cached at the edge.
A request served from an edge cache without contacting the origin.

nodes.title: Peering, Transit Gateway, VPN, and Direct Connect cost

prompts.label: WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: What should this concept make you think of?

reveal.text: VPC peering, Transit Gateway, Site-to-Site VPN, and Direct Connect have different topology, bandwidth, operational, and data-processing cost characteristics. Cross-AZ traffic can also add data-transfer cost, so the actual traffic path matters.

prompts.label: WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: Choose topology from scale, bandwidth, and the traffic path.

items: A small number of VPCs need direct connectivity -> VPC peering can avoid a transit hub but does not provide transitive routing.
Many VPCs/hybrid networks need centralized routing -> Transit Gateway simplifies topology but adds attachment/data-processing cost.
Encrypted connectivity over the internet is acceptable -> Site-to-Site VPN.
High-volume dedicated hybrid connectivity is required -> evaluate Direct Connect against VPN/internet transfer economics.

prompts.label: EXAM CLUE
prompts.placeholder: What phrase should make this answer jump out?

items: few VPCs / direct pair -> peering
many networks / central hub -> Transit Gateway
encrypted internet tunnel -> VPN
dedicated high-volume hybrid link -> Direct Connect

source_refs.title: AWS Certified Solutions Architect - Associate (SAA-C03) exam guide

glossary.definition: Traffic that crosses Availability Zone boundaries and can create additional data-transfer cost depending on the services and path.
A central routing architecture that replaces many point-to-point network connections with a shared hub.

nodes.title: Cost Explorer, Budgets, Data Exports/CUR, and allocation tags

prompts.label: WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: What should this concept make you think of?

reveal.text: Cost Explorer is for interactive cost/usage analysis and trends. AWS Budgets tracks budget thresholds and forecasts. CUR/CUR 2.0 provides detailed billing and usage data; AWS Data Exports is the recommended way to create CUR 2.0 exports. Cost Explorer can also show amortized cost views for commitment-aware analysis. Activated cost allocation tags help attribute spend to teams, products, or environments.

prompts.label: WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: Choose the cost tool from the analysis need.

items: Explore and group historical spend interactively -> Cost Explorer.
Alert on actual or forecasted threshold -> AWS Budgets.
Need detailed line-item billing data for custom analysis -> CUR 2.0 / Data Exports.
Need project/team/environment attribution -> activate and use cost allocation tags.

prompts.label: EXAM CLUE
prompts.placeholder: What phrase should make this answer jump out?

items: interactive trend -> Cost Explorer
threshold / forecast alert -> Budgets
detailed billing dataset -> CUR 2.0 / Data Exports
attribute spend -> cost allocation tags

nodes.title: Network throttling and bandwidth cost controls

prompts.label: WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: How can request rate and bandwidth choices affect network-related cost?

reveal.text: Cost optimization can limit unnecessary consumption before it reaches expensive downstream resources. API Gateway throttling controls steady request rate and a burst limit. Hybrid links should also be sized from required throughput instead of automatically purchasing the highest bandwidth option.

prompts.label: COMPARE
prompts.placeholder: Match the cost problem to the control.

cells.problem: Unexpected client bursts overload downstream APIs

cells.control: Evaluate multiple VPN paths/Transit Gateway ECMP or a dedicated link

cells.problem: Dedicated hybrid bandwidth is substantially overprovisioned
cells.control: Right-size Direct Connect bandwidth to measured need

prompts.label: EXAM CLUE
prompts.placeholder: What wording should trigger these controls?

items: request burst -> throttle rate/burst
hybrid throughput requirement -> size bandwidth
do not overprovision network capacity without measured need

source_refs.title: AWS Certified Solutions Architect - Associate (SAA-C03) exam guide
Throttle requests to REST APIs in API Gateway

glossary.definition: Limiting request rate or burst capacity to protect downstream resources and control resource consumption.
The short-term request burst target allowed before throttling begins.
The amount of network data that can be transferred per unit of time.
